Upstate. Downstate. One Big Red.

With deep roots in Ithaca and a rapidly expanding footprint in New York City, no other institution connects upstate and downstate New York quite like Cornell. Cornellians have more opportunities for learning, discovery and engagement than ever before.

Planning travel to Ithaca or New York City?

Find resources to make a single visit or regular trips easier and more effective.

Transportation Lodging Reserving Space Technology Library Resources

You have a range of options for traveling between our Ithaca and New York City campuses or getting around either location.

Intercampus Travel

  • Cornell’s Campus-to-Campus Bus Service – Exceptional, express service between Cornell’s Ithaca and NYC campuses, seven days a week.
  • Rental Vehicles and Charters – Cornell-approved options for renting or chartering vehicles for faculty and staff travel.
  • Personal Vehicle Use – Requirements for driving personal vehicles for university business.
  • Ithaca Tompkins International Airport – Offering connecting flights for domestic and international travel.
  • Airlines – Cornell-negotiated air travel discounts may be available.

Local Transportation

Ithaca

  • Ithaca Carshare – Local car-share rentals on an hourly basis, available 24/7.
  • Tompkins Consolidated Area Transit (TCAT) – Local bus service connecting campus, Ithaca and the surrounding area. Faculty and staff ride for free with their Cornell ID.

New York City

  • Metropolitan Transit Authority (MTA) – Bus, subway and commuter rail options serving the NYC metro area.
  • NJ Transit – Bus, train and light rail service between New Jersey and NYC.
  • NYC Ferry – Service to the Cornell Tech campus on Roosevelt Island as well as parts of Manhattan, Queens and Brooklyn.
  • Roosevelt Island Tramway – Fast, convenient service between Roosevelt Island and Manhattan.

Whether staying overnight or for an extended trip, there are a variety of accommodations conveniently located on or near our campuses.

Ithaca

  • The Statler Hotel – Located in the heart of Cornell’s campus, the Statler is an innovative leader in hospitality.
  • Off-Campus Rental Listing – Searchable database of available off-campus rentals.
  • Temporary Housing Options – On-campus housing options for qualifying visiting faculty members and Cornell affiliates.
  • Live in Ithaca – The Tompkins Chamber highlights careers, community and quality of life in the Ithaca area.

New York City

  • The Cornell Club-New York – Located in Midtown Manhattan, the club accepts memberships from faculty and staff of Cornell and affiliate schools.
  • Graduate by Hilton-New York – A hotel located on the Cornell Tech campus on Roosevelt Island.
  • WCM Short-Term Housing – Resources on finding sublets and furnished apartments in NYC.
  • Helmsley Medical Tower Guest Suites – Lodging options for NewYork-Presbyterian affiliates.
  • Off-Campus Student Housing – Resources for off-campus accommodations, including NYC-based housing options offered by other universities and partners.

Cornell provides a host of spaces for meetings, events or simply a quiet place to work when visiting Ithaca and NYC. For full details, review the space reservation and use policies.

Ithaca

  • Event Scheduling Tool – Access the 25Live tool to reserve space for events. Allow at least five business days for approval.
  • Event Planning at Cornell – Everything you need to know about requirements, processes, procedures and appropriate use of spaces at Cornell.

New York City

  • 570 Lexington Avenue – Cornell’s Midtown hub for faculty research, student learning and public engagement activities.
  • Cornell Tech – The Tata Innovation Center and Emma Georgina Bloomberg Center may be reserved for events and activities.
  • Cornell SC Johnson College of Business – To reserve the event and meeting space at 45 W. 57th Street, 5th floor, contact Andrea Rose: arose@cornell.edu.
  • AAP NYC – To reserve the event and meeting space in Lower Manhattan at 26 Broadway, 20th floor, contact Bob Balder: rwb43@cornell.edu.

Tools to stay connected and resources to support your work when traveling off campus.

Video Conferencing

  • Zoom – Free access to online meetings and webinars from your computer or mobile device. Open to Cornell faculty, staff and students with a NetID or Weill Cornell Medicine CWID.

Data Management

  • Box – A free service for convenient file storage and sharing. Log in with NetID or Weill Cornell Medicine CWID.
  • Cornell Secure File Transfer – A secure method for sending and receiving files, open to anyone with a NetID.
  • CU VPN – Use Cornell’s virtual private network (VPN) to connect to campus resources that would otherwise be unavailable from distant networks, such as file servers and print services.

Wireless Network Access

  • Wi-Fi – All Cornell campuses in Ithaca and NYC offer the eduroam secure Wi-Fi network, accessible to registered faculty, staff, students and affiliates with the same credentials between campuses. These privileges extend to all eduroam-connected institutions. Visitors may register to use the Cornell-Visitor network at Ithaca or Cornell Tech and the WCMCGuest network at Weill Cornell Medicine.

Technical Support

  • For help with technical issues, contact IT@Cornell in Ithaca, Cornell Tech IT or Weill Cornell Medicine ITS.

Cornell University Library (CUL) provides a variety of resources to meet faculty, student and staff needs away from home.

Travel Resources

  • Off-Campus Access – Connect to CUL databases and other resources from your computer or mobile device at any time.
  • Visitor Privileges – Cornell’s libraries are open to all. Contact the Library Public Services Office for more details.
  • Library Services – Everything you need to know about borrowing materials, accessing equipment and services, visiting online or in person and more.

Ithaca

  • Eighteen libraries are available in Ithaca to support your research, learning and practice. View the full list of libraries, hours, contact information and more.

New York City

  • Weill Cornell Medicine Samuel J. Wood Library – Cornell faculty, staff and students enjoy borrowing privileges and librarian support with a current Cornell ID.
  • Cornell Tech Library Services – A guide to accessing library services while visiting Cornell Tech. Contact cutech-library@cornell.edu.
  • Columbia Library Borrowing Privileges (2CUL) – A reciprocal borrowing program for current students, faculty and staff of Cornell and Columbia.
  • New York Public Library – Anyone who lives, works, attends school or pays property taxes in New York state can access the library system across the Bronx, Manhattan and Staten Island.

Welcome to Cornell!

Established in 1865, Cornell University is a privately endowed research university and a partner of the State University of New York. Unique within the Ivy League, we make contributions in all fields of knowledge in a manner that prioritizes public engagement to help improve the quality of life in our state, the nation and the world.

Visiting the Campus

Visitor Relations is the front door to exploring Cornell’s Ithaca campus, providing information and tours to prospective students and families, alumni and Ithaca area visitors. Situated in a central location with stunning views of Beebe Lake, the Martin Y. Tang Welcome Center is the perfect place to start your campus experience.

Martin Y. Tang Welcome Center
616 Thurston Avenue, Ithaca, N.Y. 14850
Mon - Fri, 8 a.m. - 5 p.m. | Sat, 8 a.m. - 3 p.m. (closed on Saturdays in December and January)

Welcome Center Building closed to the public July 3-5, 2026, September 7, November 25-29, December 21, 2026 through January 18, 2027.

Visitor Relations staff are available to assist and answer general questions: (607) 254-4636 (INFO) or info@cornell.edu.

Touring the Ithaca Campus

Connect with Current Students

Join a student-led tour and experience all that Cornell has to offer. Capacity is limited, so advance registration is required. In-person campus tours are geared toward the undergraduate student experience and last roughly 75 minutes. Tours are held rain or shine, so please dress appropriately.

Self-guided campus tour

Discover campus on your own through a step-by-step self-guided tour via your smartphone. Our general campus tour lasts approximately one hour and covers the heart of campus.

Virtual Tour

Can’t visit in person? Explore the beauty and traditions of campus from anywhere through our virtual tour – available for desktop or mobile devices.

Special Group Tour Requests

Special group tours may be arranged during select times of year with three weeks advance notice. Due to high demand of tour requests, we are unable to accommodate walk-in groups, but are happy to assist with directions, dining options, and campus information. For more information about available dates and fees, please email specialtours@cornell.edu.

Prospective Undergraduate Students

Applying to Cornell

The first step to becoming a Cornellian is applying for admission. Start your journey by reviewing our admissions timeline, process and requirements and meeting our students.

Information Sessions

Cornell's undergraduate admissions community offers in-person information sessions and a variety of virtual resources that provide unique insight into student life, the admissions process and admissions requirements. Consider watching our on-demand general information session before diving deeper into college- and school-specific sessions.

Contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions at (607) 255-5241 or admissions@cornell.edu for more details about our admissions sessions.

Cornell in a Day

Experience Cornell's Ithaca campus through a series of photographs that showcase its vibrant community, ongoing opportunities and natural beauty at every turn, all day long.

Getting to Campus

Nestled in New York’s Finger Lakes region, Ithaca is only a few hours away from New York City, Philadelphia, Toronto, Boston and other major metropolitan areas.

Follow the travel guides below, or use your preferred online navigation tool to find directions to the Martin Y. Tang Welcome Center (616 Thurston Ave., Ithaca, N.Y.)

From Syracuse and other points northeast:

Take Interstate 81 south toward Cortland, then Route 13 south to Route 366 toward campus.

From Auburn and other points north:

Take Route 34 south, then follow Triphammer Road south to campus.

From Albany, New England and other points east:

Follow the New York State Thruway through Albany to Interstate 88 west, then take exit 8 in Bainbridge. Follow Route 206 west to Whitney Point, then Route 79 west toward Ithaca.

From Philadelphia and other points south:

Follow Interstate 476 north to Scranton, Pa., then continue on Interstate 81 north through Binghamton, N.Y. Continue northward on I-81 to exit 8 at Whitney Point, then follow Route 79 west to Ithaca.

From New York City:

Follow Interstate 80 west to Stroudsburg, Pa., then continue on Interstate 81 north toward Binghamton, N.Y. Continue northward on I-81 to exit 8 at Whitney Point, then follow Route 79 west to Ithaca.

From Rochester, Buffalo and points west:

Follow the New York State Thruway (Interstate 90) east toward exit 42 in Geneva, then take Route 96 south toward Ithaca.

Ithaca Tompkins International Airport is a 10-minute drive from campus and offers connecting flights for domestic and international travel. Currently, Delta Airlines provides round-trip service twice daily to John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City, and United Airlines provides round-trip service twice daily to Dulles International Airport in Washington D.C. Effective October 1, 2025, a third round-trip flight will be available to Dulles International Airport. Ground transportation options include rental cars, public transportation, ride hailing apps, taxi service, and complimentary shuttles to and from many hotels.

Additional airports within driving distance to campus:

  • Syracuse Hancock International Airport/SYR (75 minutes by car from Cornell’s campus)
  • Elmira Corning Regional Airport/ELM (50 minutes by car from Cornell’s campus)
  • Greater Binghamton Airport/BGM (55 minutes by car from Cornell’s campus)
  • Frederick Douglass Rochester International Airport/ROC (110 minutes by car from Cornell’s campus)
  • Buffalo Niagara International Airport/BUF (150 minutes by car from Cornell’s campus)

Cornell offers direct bus service from Ithaca to New York City via the Campus-to-Campus bus.

Visitor Information

Parking

Parking is available for a nominal fee on weekdays and for free on the weekends. You may choose to pay for parking in advance while scheduling your tour or pay to use any number of conveniently located Parkmobile lots once on campus.

Public Transit

TCAT (Tompkins Consolidated Area Transit) provides fast and affordable bus transit throughout campus, downtown Ithaca and Tompkins County. Daily cash fares start at $1.50 per trip; children 13 and younger ride for free. Visit tcatbus.com for schedules, maps and more details.

Campus Accessibility

Cornell is committed to maintaining an accessible, usable and welcoming environment for all faculty, staff, students and visitors. Cornell offers a detailed map of accessibility points and gender-neutral restrooms; more information and resources may be found at the Disability Access page.

Dining

Focused on diverse, healthy and sustainable cuisine, dining at Cornell is a culinary experience rarely found on a college campus.

Campus Venues

Every week, Cornell plays host to dozens of lectures, performances, exhibits and much more. Below are just a few of the many locations often visited by the public. Check out events.cornell.edu for a full list of upcoming events and activities, or the "Life at Cornell" page to explore more opportunities for enrichment.

Around Ithaca and the Finger Lakes Region

Beyond campus, take advantage of a wide variety of entertainment, dining, lodging and recreation options. The Visit Ithaca website has up-to-date listings, details on upcoming events, and even a list of local waterfalls.

Our Profile

Cornell is a privately endowed research university and a partner of the State University of New York. As the federal land-grant institution in New York State, we have a responsibility—unique within the Ivy League—to make contributions in all fields of knowledge in a manner that prioritizes public engagement to help improve the quality of life in our state, the nation, the world.

Cornell Through the Years

More than 150 years of excellence in education, research and public engagement have given Cornell a unique history that is rich with innovation and tradition.

1865
Cornell charter signed into law

NY State Senate passes the bill that establishes Cornell University on April 27.

1868
Cornell chimes ring for the first time

The original set of nine bells first rings out at the university's opening ceremonies.

1901
Architecture students stage first 'Dragon Day'

Inspired by an idea from Willard Dickerman Straight 1901, the first Dragon Day is held.

1977
Voyager spacecraft launches

Cornell astronomers and astrophysicists are extensively involved in the missions of Voyager 1 and 2 to explore the outer solar system.

1915
Cornell Lab of O takes wing

The Cornell Laboratory of Ornithology is established.

As the federal land-grant institution in New York State, we have a responsibility—unique within the Ivy League—to make contributions in all fields of knowledge in a manner that prioritizes public engagement to help improve the quality of life in our state, the nation, the world. Public Engagement University Factbook --> Cornell Through the Years More than 150 years of excellence in education, research and public engagement have given Cornell a unique history that is rich with innovation and tradition. 1865 Cornell charter signed into law NY State Senate passes the bill that establishes Cornell University on April 27. 1868 Cornell chimes ring for the first time The original set of nine bells first rings out at the university's opening ceremonies. 1901 Architecture students stage first 'Dragon Day' Inspired by an idea from Willard Dickerman Straight 1901, the first Dragon Day is held. 1977 Voyager spacecraft launches Cornell astronomers and astrophysicists are extensively involved in the missions of Voyager 1 and 2 to explore the outer solar system. 1915 Cornell Lab of O takes wing The Cornell Laboratory of Ornithology is established.
